lens: Linus — taste, simplicity, kill ceremony, prefer deletion
answer: Reviewed PR #17 (head review/multispectrum-9-prs-final, +7639/-0, 173 files). The mechanical claim holds: 9 merged PRs (#1,#2,#3,#5,#6,#7,#8,#9,#11) x ~9 facets x 2 rounds + 9 synthesis = ~171 evidence JSONs, plus audit-chain.jsonl +9 lines and FixupTasks. r1 files contain substantive per-PR content (e.g., pr-12-F1-r1 has 9 concrete key_claims, 5 anti_patterns, file:line citations — real review work). r2 files are the smell. Sampling pr-1-F2-r2 vs pr-1-F3-r2 (via PR diff) shows the two files are byte-identical modulo facet_id/facet_name/reviewer_id: same three 'Round-2 Fn reconciliation preserved consensus finding...' bullets, same remediation string copy-pasted ('Keep the synthesis FixupTask and do not downgrade severity without a new facet-specific evidence file.'), same naming_justification template, same rendered_at_unix=1778920055 across all eight F2-F9 r2 files. That is mechanical copy-paste rebuttal, exactly what the PR body promises NOT to do: 'Continuation validation used no shell scripts, no .mjs, and no Python.' The doctrine forces a r2 rebuttal round before synthesis (specs/cross-cutting/multispectrum-review.json defines round 2 as 'each provider sees others responses and provides rebuttals'). Here the 'rebuttal' is a string-template fill: position=concurs_with_synthesis_after_rebuttal, consensus_delta=fixed-string, round_2_findings = the same three sentences with the facet-name word swapped in. Linus take: this is evidence theater. Either (a) the r2 round was genuinely a no-op for these 8 facets and the schema should let you write {round:2, no_new_findings: true, reason: ...} once — not 8 copies of the same paragraph — or (b) the round was non-trivial and each facet should actually rebut from its own lens. Both options are honest; what was shipped is neither. The PR-policy line forbidding shell/Python/.mjs is the root anti-pattern: it forces humans to hand-type what a 30-line jq+printf script would produce identically, then calls the hand-typing 'validation rigor.' That inverts the meaning of automation. The r1 evidence is real and worth keeping; the r2 round as currently shaped is pure ceremony. The retroactive nature (reviewing 9 already-merged PRs) further confirms the ceremonial framing — no merge gate could have been informed by this. Verdict: approve-with-fixups against POLICY, not against this PR (already merged). Fixups land on the r2-rebuttal schema and the no-scripts rule.
key_claims: PR #17 adds ~171 evidence JSONs covering 9 merged PRs x ~9 facets x 2 rounds plus synthesis; r1 files contain substantive per-PR review content (e.g., pr-12-F1-r1 has 9 key_claims with file:line citations).

r2 rebuttal files for the same PR across facets F2-F9 are byte-identical modulo facet_id/facet_name/reviewer_id; verified by extracting pr-1-F2-r2 and pr-1-F3-r2 from /tmp/oya-msr-pr12-18/pr-17.diff and confirming identical round_2_findings text, identical remediation string, identical naming_justification template, identical rendered_at_unix=1778920055.

The three round_2_findings bullets are introduced by the literal prefix 'Round-2 Fn reconciliation preserved consensus finding:' with the facet letter swapped — a string-template fill, not a per-lens rebuttal.

The remediation field for every round_2_finding is the same sentence: 'Keep the synthesis FixupTask and do not downgrade severity without a new facet-specific evidence file.' That is not facet-specific advice.

The PR body §Policy declares 'Continuation validation used no shell scripts, no .mjs, and no Python' — which forces hand-typed boilerplate when the same artifacts could be produced (transparently and reproducibly) by a ~30-line jq+printf generator.

The doctrine spec (specs/cross-cutting/multispectrum-review.json) requires r2 as 'each provider sees others responses and provides rebuttals'; the shipped r2 round_2_findings carry no rebuttal — they copy the r1/synthesis position with a fixed prefix.
Retroactive evidence wave for 9 already-merged PRs cannot have informed any merge gate; this is provenance/audit-trail work, not review-loop work, and should be honestly framed as such.
r1 evidence (where reviewers actually applied a lens) is high-signal and should be kept; the cost-of-ceremony complaint is scoped to the r2 boilerplate and the no-scripts policy that produced it.
uncertainty_areas: Whether the multispectrum-review.json schema permits a single aggregate 'r2 no-change' artifact per PR; if it requires one r2 file per facet unconditionally, the schema itself is the smell rather than this PR.

Whether the no-scripts rule in the PR §Policy is a one-off author convention or encoded in repo doctrine (feedback_*.md); a doctrine-level ban on generators would explain the hand-typing but would be the deeper anti-pattern.

Whether other r1 files across the wave match the substance of pr-12-F1-r1 (sampled) or degrade toward the r2 template shape for the less-deep facets; a full sweep across all r1 files was not performed in this single-lens pass.
anti_patterns_detected: evidence-theater-r2-rebuttal: 8 facet r2 files per PR are byte-identical modulo id fields; the 'rebuttal' is a fixed string with the facet name swapped, not a per-lens reconsideration.

policy-forces-hand-typing: PR §Policy bans shell/Python/.mjs for continuation validation, forcing humans to hand-type artifacts a 30-line generator would produce identically and reproducibly; inverts the meaning of 'rigor'.

schema-requires-ceremony-when-no-op: r2 round has no schema-sanctioned 'no new findings' shape, so reviewers manufacture findings that restate r1/synthesis with a 'preserved consensus finding' prefix.
retroactive-evidence-framed-as-review: 9 already-merged PRs reviewed after the fact; cannot inform a merge gate; framing as 'review' rather than 'audit-trail backfill' obscures the actual purpose.

boilerplate-naming-justification: naming_justification field across all 171 files is a templated string referencing 'the multispectrum evidence path contract' — the field exists to force per-file thought and instead carries identical text.

findings.summary: r2 rebuttal files across facets F2-F9 for the same PR are byte-identical modulo id fields; round_2_findings carry a fixed 'Round-2 Fn reconciliation preserved consensus finding' string with no per-lens rebuttal content.
findings.recommended_action: Extend the multispectrum-review.json r2 schema to allow {round: 2, no_new_findings: true, reason: <string>, supersedes_r1: false} as a sanctioned no-op shape; emit ONE per-PR aggregate r2 artifact when no facet has new content, instead of N per-facet copies of the same paragraph.

findings.summary: PR §Policy 'Continuation validation used no shell scripts, no .mjs, and no Python' forces humans to hand-type artifacts a small generator would produce identically; the no-scripts rule produces the very boilerplate it claims to avoid.
findings.recommended_action: Replace the blanket no-scripts rule with an allowlist: evidence-artifact emission MAY use a checked-in renderer (e.g., scripts/evidence/emit-r2.jq or similar) provided the renderer source is in the PR diff and the inputs (r1 paths, synthesis path) are explicit. Bans the opaque .mjs spaghetti while restoring the legitimate use of generators.

findings.summary: PR #17 frames retroactive evidence backfill for 9 already-merged PRs as 'multispectrum review evidence'; this conflates audit-trail provenance with the review loop and weakens the meaning of 'evidence' in the doctrine.
findings.recommended_action: Rename the path or add a marker field (e.g., retroactive: true, original_merge_window: <date_range>) on each artifact, and add a synthesis-level note explaining that these artifacts could not have informed the merge gates and exist for provenance only.
